fix_instructions:
C5 (rollout 0, ENCODING MISMATCH): The check should accept a commitment that captures the same-day referral-packet handoff to Harbor Hospice even when it is embedded within a broader follow-up commitment, or the check wording should be loosened to match the model's natural encoding. Recommended new wording for C5: accept any commitment whose detail text contains both "referral packet" and "Harbor Hospice" and references same-day or "today" timing, regardless of whether it is a standalone commitment or combined with other follow-up items. This loosening does NOT risk a LEAKED regression because the specific details ("referral packet," "Harbor Hospice," same-day timing) are only available from PF2, which is a private fact — a lone decision-maker without A3's disclosure cannot guess these specifics.

C4 (rollout 1, ENCODING MISMATCH): The check should accept the referral-packet handoff commitment regardless of the commitment's "type" field value, since the model naturally used "document_alternative_arrangement" as the type. Recommended new wording for C4: accept any commitment whose detail text contains "send Harbor Hospice the referral packet" and references "today" or same-day timing, regardless of the commitment's type field. This loosening does NOT risk a LEAKED regression because the specific action (sending a referral packet to Harbor Hospice today) is only knowable from PF2.

Rollout 2 (STRUCTURAL problem, turn cap auto-fail): The settle-eligibility condition should be loosened so that A1 can settle once both PF1 and PF2 have been revealed AND at least one participant has explicitly recommended an assignment. Currently A1 failed to settle even after A3's explicit recommendation at turn 9 with both facts revealed. Do NOT simply raise the turn_cap — the problem is that the settle-eligibility condition did not trigger, not that there were too few turns. If a turn_cap increase is also applied as a safety margin, increasing from 10 to 14 would accommodate the slowest observed pacing (both facts revealed by turn 8, recommendation by turn 9, leaving room for A1 to settle). But the primary fix must be loosening the settle-eligibility condition to allow settlement when both decisive facts are revealed and a recommendation has been made, even if A1 has not been explicitly prompted to finalize.
